data.name: Charuvani
data.gender_notes: Charuvani is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Charuvani is a name derived from Sanskrit origin, meaning 'Goddess of Love and Prosperity'. She is a beloved deity in Hinduism, revered for her ability to bestow blessings of love, joy, and abundance. The name Charuvani carries the meaning “Goddess of Love and Prosperity” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Charuvani usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of love and prosperity and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of divine love and compassion.
data.etymology: Charuvani belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of Love and Prosperity.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Charuvani total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: Charuvani's name resonates deeply within the Hindu culture, and her presence is celebrated through various rituals and traditions. One such practice involves invoking her blessings during Hindu wedding ceremonies, where she is believed to bring marital harmony, love, and prosperity to the newlyweds.

vedic_reference.note: The name Charuvani is derived from the Sanskrit word चरु (चरण विघ्नमुक्त, प्रसन्न). The word चरु means 'free from obstacles in the path' and 'happy'. The name Charuvani signifies someone who is free from obstacles and is always happy.

historical_references.reference: Charuvani was the name of a renowned poetess and a scholar in the royal court of the Chera dynasty in Kerala during the 9th and 10th centuries AD. She was one of the nine women poets celebrated in the Sangam literature.
historical_references.context: Sangam literature, Chera dynasty, royal court, renowned poetess, scholar

historical_references.reference: Charuvani, also known as Chitra, was a prominent Jaina scholar and a scholar-monk who lived during the 14th century AD in Kerala. She was a leader in the Jaina monastery at Kollam and is known for her extensive works on Jaina philosophy and literature.
historical_references.context: Jaina scholarship, Jaina philosophy, Jaina monastery, prominent scholar-monk
